bugs_found_and_fixed.name: point_in_time_leakage
bugs_found_and_fixed.description: dim_content is a single latest-state snapshot (export date 2026-07-03), not point-in-time. days_since_last_update/content_age_days were computed against a decision point (March 15) using update/creation dates that could be AFTER that point, leaking future information.
bugs_found_and_fixed.fix: dropped rows where days_since_last_update < 0 or content_age_days < 0

bugs_found_and_fixed.name: nondeterministic_remote_row_order
bugs_found_and_fixed.description: DuckDB does not guarantee row order on a remote parquet scan without ORDER BY, so .unique() and argsort tie-breaking were not actually deterministic despite a fixed numpy seed -- reruns produced different comparison tables.
bugs_found_and_fixed.fix: sorted the client list before seeding the shuffle; used np.argsort(..., kind='stable') with a fixed row order (sorted by content_hash_id) for precision_at_k
bugs_found_and_fixed.verification: 3 independent full reruns (A/B/C) produced identical results

bugs_found_and_fixed.name: baseline_never_fires_on_test_set
bugs_found_and_fixed.description: The rescaled stale_but_visible baseline scored 0 of 1979 test rows above zero on the held-out client slice -- an all-tied, all-zero score array. Precision@K from it would measure row sort order, not the rule.
bugs_found_and_fixed.fix: precision_at_k returns None (reported as N/A) when fewer than 1 score is nonzero, instead of a misleading number

baseline_rescaled_rule.note: never fires on test set (0/1979 rows score > 0)

chosen_model_rationale: wins at P@50 (0.64 vs 0.46), loses narrowly at P@20 (0.60 vs 0.65); feature importances are directly readable, unlike reasoning about 8 interacting logistic coefficients

errors.false_positive_pattern: high-impression pages (4,461-16,986) flagged confidently (0.65-0.78) that turned out fine
errors.false_negative_pattern: low-volume pages (54-283 impressions) the model was uncertain about (0.32-0.35) that did decline

limitations: test set is small: 1,979 rows across only 6 clients -- results describe this run, not a guaranteed property of the lane
staleness (days_since_last_update) carries almost no weight in the winning model, consistent with Week 4's MIXED verdict on the same signal
next step (Week 6 validation audit) should stress-test the client-holdout precision rather than take it at face value
